claim: Brantwood, John Ruskin's lakeside home, charges £16.50 adult, £13.75 student, free for under-16s, with house 10:30-16:00 and gardens to 16:30; £1 discount with Gondola or Coniston Launch ticket.
quote: Adults: £16.50 Students: £13.75 Children (16 and under): FREE ... House: 10:30 AM – 4:00 PM Gardens: 10:30 AM – 4:30 PM ... A £1 discount applies with Gondola or Coniston Launch tickets.

claim: Brantwood opens every day in summer, Wednesday to Sunday in winter, with free parking, no pre-booking needed and a 250-acre estate of eight gardens.
quote: Brantwood is open every day during summer and Wednesday to Sunday during winter ... No pre-booking required, Free parking for visitors ... The 250-acre estate features eight gardens with varying levels of gradient.

claim: The National Trust Steam Yacht Gondola offers three routes — 45-minute Mountain, ~1-hour Heart of the Lake, and 1h 45m Full Lake — departing from the right-hand jetty at Coniston Boating Centre, bookable up to 4 weeks ahead.
quote: Mountain Cruise: 45 minutes ... Heart of the Lake: approximately one hour ... Full Lake Cruise: one hour and 45 minutes ... Gondola operates from the right-hand jetty at Coniston Boating Centre ... up to four weeks in advance.

claim: Gondola Mountain Cruise costs £13 adult / £6.50 child, Full Lake Cruise £23.50 / £11.75, with NT members getting 10% off, and the steamer typically sails April–October Tue/Wed/Thu/Sat.
quote: The Mountain Cruise costs £13 for adults and £6.50 for children (family £32.50), while the Full Lake Cruise is £23.50 for adults and £11.75 for children (family £58.75) ... Gondola sails April - October on Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday and Saturday.

claim: Coniston Launch — a separate operator from the Gondola — runs Red (£18 adult), Yellow/Wild Cat Island (£20 adult, hop-on/off across red+yellow) and Green Southern themed (£22 adult) day-ticket routes, with under-5s free.
quote: Red Route ... Adults (16+): £18.00 ... Yellow Route (Wild Cat Island Cruise) ... Adults (16+): £20.00 ... Green Route (Southern Lake Themed Cruise) ... Adults (16+): £22.00 ... the yellow route will allow you to hop on and off the boat for the whole day, on either of the yellow or red routes.

claim: Coniston Launch operates its main timetable 7 March to 1 November 2026 with a reduced winter service afterwards, and a 15% online discount is available.
quote: The service runs from 7 March – 1 November 2026, with extended service from 2 November 2026 – 5 March 2027 ... A 15% discount is available when you buy tickets online.

claim: Hill Top, Beatrix Potter's tiny farmhouse at Near Sawrey, requires pre-booked timed-entry tickets for everyone including NT members, at £17–£18.70 adult, with a 2-hour car park stay and 10:00–17:00 opening on open days.
quote: Pre‑booking is required for everyone, including National Trust members ... Adult (18+): £17.00-£18.70 ... Car park has a maximum 2-hour stay and closes at 5:30pm ... House, garden, and shop all operate 10:00-17:00 during open days.

claim: Hill Top tickets are released in batches roughly two weeks ahead and sell out quickly, with the car park limited and unable to accommodate campervans.
quote: Tickets can be booked up to two weeks in advance and right up to a few minutes before each slot ... Campervans and motorhomes cannot be accommodated.

claim: The former Beatrix Potter Gallery in Hawkshead — gifted to the NT by Potter's solicitor husband William Heelis — has been reimagined as Tabitha Twitchit's Bookshop, open 10:30–16:30 with no admission fee.
quote: The former Beatrix Potter Gallery has been reimagined as a second-hand bookshop ... is now reopened as Tabitha Twitchit's Bookshop ... 10:30 AM to 4:30 PM ... It was gifted to the National Trust by William Heelis—Beatrix Potter's husband.

claim: The Tarn Hows circular walk is a 2-mile (3.2 km) firm gravel loop suitable for wheelchairs and pushchairs, with free Tramper mobility-scooter loans bookable 48 hours ahead.
quote: Distance: 2 miles (3.2 km) ... a firm gravel path around the tarn with some climbs and descents, suitable for pushchairs, prams, buggies, wheelchairs and mobility vehicles ... All-terrain Tramper mobility scooters are available to borrow at no charge.

claim: Tarn Hows car park is free to NT members; non-members pay £7 for up to 2 hours, £8.50 for 2–4 hours or £10 all day, with blue-badge holders free.
quote: Parking is free for Members; charges for non-members are 0-2 Hours £7, 2-4 Hours £8.50, and All day £10 ... Blue badge holders park for free.

claim: Grizedale Forest hosts the UK's largest forest sculpture exhibition with multiple waymarked walking trails, Cafe Ambio open 10–17, and pay-on-exit ANPR parking at £2.90 for the first hour, £14 max all-day.
quote: unique sculptures which are dotted throughout the forest ... Up to 20 minutes: No charge ... First hour: £2.90 ... All day maximum charge: £14 ... Cafe Ambio ... Hours match visitor center operations (10am-5pm daily).

claim: Go Ape Grizedale offers Zip Trekking Adventure (from £55) and Forest Segway (from £28), though storm damage has closed the Treetop Challenge high-ropes until spring 2026.
quote: Zip Trekking Adventure prices from £55 ... Forest Segway prices from £28 ... Due to storm damage Treetop Challenge at Go Ape Grizedale is now closed until spring 2026.

claim: Hawkshead's traffic-free village centre includes the 17th-century Old Grammar School museum where William Wordsworth was educated 1779–1787 and carved his name into a still-preserved desk.
quote: William Wordsworth attended Hawkshead Grammar School from 1787 ... the downstairs schoolroom has not changed much since Wordsworth's day - you can sit at the desk where he carved his name ... Cars are prohibited from the village centre, with a car park conveniently located just outside.
